title: A single-family --preserve-source-ids retry leaves the other families behind, and the human-readable output never says so
description:
FOUND 2026-09-17 while answering quest-cli's open design question about multi-family sources (their QCLI-322). This is a gap in what LCLI-466 SHIPPED, found by its own author session after the fact, not a pre-existing one -- LCLI-466 made it materially easier to reach.

THE PATH. LCLI-466 taught the wizard to catch Quest's default-mode alias collision and offer a --preserve-source-ids retry, prompting for the family with a default pre-filled from the id Quest quoted. The prompt says "Which Backlog id family should be imported (one family per run, e.g. LCLI)?". Quest imports ONE family per run -- its own "migration backlog preview --help" says so explicitly ("a backlog holding more than one, e.g. LCLI and LORE, imports one family per run"), and src/adapters/quest.ts:183-185 already documents it.

So on a two-family Backlog the shipped flow is: collision -> accept the retry -> answer LCLI -> the LCLI family migrates and the other family does not. Before LCLI-466 the same operator got a bare exit 5 and had to go read flag documentation, which at least put the one-family-per-run sentence in front of them. The improved UX walks them into a partial import faster. That is the honest way to state it.

WHY IT IS SILENT, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL DEFECT. Quest reports it: the receipt carries a survivors array, Lore carries it through TrackerMigrationResult (src/tracker-migration.ts:21,130) into the --json envelope, and docs/reference/cli-surface.md:219 documents survivors as part of that output. But the HUMAN-READABLE renderers print only "migration: <state>, <n> mapped (<digest>)" -- src/commands/init.ts:2077 and :2136. The survivors array is rendered nowhere.

And --json is one of the three vetoes that disables the wizard entirely (it must never prompt on a machine-readable run). So the operator who can reach this path is BY CONSTRUCTION the one who cannot see the field that would warn them. The data is captured, carried, and documented; it just never reaches the only person who needs it.

THIS REPOSITORY IS THE EXISTENCE PROOF, so this is not reasoning from a help string. lore-cli's own Backlog held two families. CLAUDE.md records the cutover: 425 records migrated, and 297 excluded LORE-family records "all proven non-unique and removed at commit f84f586". One project, two families, one run -- and it took a human reasoning about the excluded family afterward.

WHAT TO DECIDE RATHER THAN ASSUME. Surfacing survivors in the human renderer is the floor, not necessarily the answer. The stronger fix is to ask BEFORE applying: the preservation-mode preview knows what it is about to import, so the wizard could say "this will import LCLI and leave N LORE records behind -- continue?" rather than reporting it afterwards. Prefer the version that removes the surprise over the one that documents it, per the fleet's standing preference. Whether the flag path (non-interactive) should also warn, and on which stream, is part of the decision.

CROSS-REPO: quest-cli recorded the multi-family question as an open DESIGN CALL rather than resolving it (QCLI-322), and asked for a real consumer case. This case has been sent to them, with the preference that a per-family answer beats a single boolean -- a boolean answered for the colliding record's family alone would still walk an operator into the partial import, just more confidently. Their side may or may not change; this task does not depend on it, because the survivors data already exists today.

ACCEPTANCE SHAPE: a wizard run against a genuinely multi-family Backlog that hits a collision, takes the retry, and imports one family must tell the operator -- in human-readable output, not only in --json -- that records were left behind and roughly what they are. Proven against a real two-family repro with real backlog+quest binaries, not only a unit test, since the whole defect is that the information exists everywhere except in front of the person.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A wizard run against a genuinely multi-family Backlog that hits the alias-collision retry and imports one family tells the operator, in human-readable output (not only --json), that records from the other family were left behind and roughly what/how many

The stronger fix is chosen unless a documented reason rules it out: ask before applying (preview knows what it is about to import, so warn and let the operator confirm/abort) rather than only reporting survivors after the fact, per the fleet preference for removing surprise over documenting it
Whether the non-interactive/flag path (--json, --yes, etc.) also warns, and on which stream, is decided and implemented consistently with the interactive case rather than left silent by omission
Proven against a real two-family Backlog + real quest binary repro (not only a unit test), since the defect is that survivors data exists everywhere except in front of the operator

plan: 1. Read src/commands/init.ts around the collision retry flow and the human-readable renderers at (roughly) :2077 and :2136, plus src/tracker-migration.ts TrackerMigrationResult/survivors and src/adapters/quest.ts
2. Decide pre-apply-warn vs post-apply-report per the fleet preference (prefer pre-apply); record the decision and why on the task
3. Implement: surface survivors count/ids in the human-readable renderer, and add the pre-apply warning/confirmation if chosen
4. Decide + implement the non-interactive/flag-path behavior (which stream, still runs or requires an explicit ack)
5. Build a real two-family Backlog scratch repro (real backlog+quest binaries) exercising the collision -> retry -> partial import path; confirm the warning/report appears
6. Update docs/reference/cli-surface.md if the documented survivors/output shape changes
7. npm run check exits 0; lore check exits 0 if docs touched
implementationNotes:
CORRECTED THE TASK'S OWN PREMISE FIRST: `survivors` (on Quest's apply/status receipt) is NOT "what got left behind" -- it is receipt-only idempotency bookkeeping, the set of target ids that exist as a result of an apply (whether written this run or already present from an earlier resumed one). On a normal successful run it tracks `mappings` almost exactly. Verified two ways: reading quest-cli's own source (src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts, BacklogPreview's own doc comment: "Records left behind... Only present in preservation mode" -- naming a DIFFERENT field) and a real quest 0.7.1 apply against a real two-family repro, whose receipt returned `"survivors":["LCLI-1","LCLI-2","LCLI-3"]` -- the imported family, not the excluded one. The field that actually means "left behind" is `excluded`, on Quest's PREVIEW response, preservation-mode only, and it was already being discarded by adapters/quest.ts's migrationPreview() parser (which read only sourceFingerprint/digest/mappings/requiresApproval). This matters because `quest migration backlog preview --help`'s own "fields" list does not mention `excluded` either -- undersold the real response, same lesson as LCLI-504/508's "declared version vs installed bytes": verify against the live binary, not the doc string, and `quest --help` resolving on a two-word command is not the same as it enumerating every field the JSON envelope actually carries.

DECISION (AC#2): implemented the STRONGER fix, not just the floor -- pre-apply warn-and-confirm in the wizard, plus post-hoc surfacing in the final summary as a second, independent layer (both, not either/or; matches the existing pattern in this file of "neither replaces the other"). This was reachable ONLY because `excluded` turned out to be on the PREVIEW (mutates nothing), not only the receipt -- had it been receipt-only, pre-apply warning would have needed Lore to independently scan the Backlog project itself (duplicating Quest's own family-grouping logic, a materially bigger and riskier change), which would have been the documented reason to fall back to post-hoc-only. That fallback was not needed here.

DECISION (AC#3, non-interactive): warn on stderr and PROCEED, never on stdout (contract: --json's stdout is the envelope alone; `migration.excluded` already carries the same data there in full). Considered and rejected: refusing outright would break an existing scripted caller who deliberately passes --source-family for a KNOWN multi-run choreography (import LCLI in run 1, LORE in run 2) -- there is no --yes-equivalent override to opt back in, so refusing what was explicitly asked for would be a straight regression with no escape hatch. Mirrors resolveScriptedBacklogRemoval's own "warn and continue, never silently" shape for the structurally analogous backlog-removal question in this same file.

IMPLEMENTATION: adapters/quest.ts gained QuestMigrationExcludedRecord + QuestMigrationPreview.excluded (optional, parsed but tolerant of absence -- a default-mode preview never sets it). tracker-migration.ts's TrackerMigrationResult gained `excluded` (always present, [] outside preservation mode), threaded through both migrateBacklogTasksToQuest branches -- the fresh preview AND the crash-recovery resume, which reads it back from the durably-recorded pending preview file rather than re-fetching (that record is exactly `QuestMigrationPreview` serialized, so it already carries `excluded` once the type gained the field). commands/init.ts: confirmFamilyExclusions (wizard) previews the chosen family a SECOND time before retryWithPreservedIds's own preview+apply -- deliberate, not an oversight: preview mutates nothing and is deterministic (verified: two consecutive real `quest migration backlog preview` calls with identical args returned the identical digest), so the extra round trip costs one local subprocess call, not correctness; assertReceipt's existing digest check is what would catch drift if it ever happened. Declining raises a fresh LoreError("denied", ...) (exit 4) -- there is no antecedent Quest refusal to re-raise here, since this branch is only reached once Quest's own preview already produced a valid plan. warnExcludedFamilies (flag path) is the non-interactive counterpart, no second preview call needed since the flag path's own single preview+apply already computed `excluded`. renderPretty/renderPlain both gained a line under the existing `migration:` summary.

REAL-BINARY PROOF (backlog 1.50.1, quest 0.7.1, bun 1.3.14, lore 0.7.0-from-source), in scratch dirs under this session's own scratchpad, never this repo's .quest. Two-family fixture used throughout: backlog with LCLI-1 (parent), LCLI-1.1 (dotted subtask under LCLI-1, positionally flattens onto a target that collides with the literal LCLI-2 -- quest task-id-prefix set to LCLI so the collision actually fires, matching LCLI-466's own "dotted subtask flattening and shifting a later allocation" cause), LCLI-2, LORE-1, LORE-2.

(1) Raw quest CLI, ground-truthing the `excluded` field before writing any parser code: `quest migration backlog preview --source . --preserve-source-ids --source-family LCLI --json` returned `"excluded":[{"sourceIdentifier":"LORE-1","family":"LORE"},{"sourceIdentifier":"LORE-2","family":"LORE"}]`; the matching `apply` returned `"survivors":["LCLI-1","LCLI-2","LCLI-3"]` (the imported set, confirming the survivors-vs-excluded correction above with a live envelope, not just source reading).

(2) Real interactive wizard over a real pty (python pty.openpty, isolated PATH containing only symlinks to bun/node/quest/backlog/git so no agent binaries leak in and trigger the unrelated multiselect step -- a first attempt that re-added a whole nvm bin dir accidentally re-exposed `codex`, which lives next to `node`/`quest` there, and hung on a step the driver didn't handle; fixed by symlinking only the five binaries actually needed). Confirm path: tracker=quest, migrate=migrate, Quest's real default-mode preview throws the real "Alias collision" (LCLI-2 vs LCLI-2), wizard offers retry, accepted, family defaults to LCLI (from the quoted id), NEW pre-apply notice printed ("Preserving Backlog ids imports one id family per run (LCLI here). 2 record(s) in LORE will NOT be imported by this run: LORE-1, LORE-2"), confirmed (y), migration applies for real (digest 47aab82f...), final pretty summary includes "migration: applied, 3 mapped (...)" followed by "2 record(s) left behind (LORE): re-run with --preserve-source-ids --source-family <PREFIX> to import them". Exit 0. Disk state after: .quest/tasks holds exactly LCLI-1/LCLI-2/LCLI-3 (LCLI-1.1 flattened to LCLI-3), no LORE-*; [tracker] backend=quest persisted.

Decline path: identical up to the new confirm, answered "n". Real output: "error: Backlog id preservation was not confirmed: 2 record(s) outside LCLI would be left behind" / "hint: answer yes to import only that family now and migrate the rest in a later run (one family per run), or resolve the alias collision in the Backlog project so a default-mode migration can import everything at once". Exit 4. Disk state after: .quest holds only workspace.toml (no tasks written at all), .lore/config.toml has no [tracker] section -- the backend is genuinely left unpinned, matching the flag-path failure precedent in this same file.

(3) Real non-interactive flag path (`lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog --preserve-source-ids --source-family LCLI`) against the same real two-family fixture, in --plain and --json separately. --plain: stderr carries the full notice (family list + ids + "run again" hint), stdout carries only "migration-excluded count=2 families=LORE" (confirmed via separate file redirection, not just eyeballing interleaved output). --json: stdout's `data.migration.excluded` is the full structured array (`[{"sourceIdentifier":"LORE-1","family":"LORE"},{"sourceIdentifier":"LORE-2","family":"LORE"}]`), `data.migration.survivors` is `["LCLI-1","LCLI-2","LCLI-3"]` -- visually confirming the two fields mean different things in one real envelope -- and stderr still carries the same human-readable notice even in --json mode (diagnostic, not payload; stdout stays pure). Exit 0 in both.

MUTATION CHECK (three mutants, each reverted after): (a) confirmFamilyExclusions's `if (excluded.length === 0) return` forced to unconditional return -> exactly 2/183 red (the wizard confirm-and-proceed test and the wizard decline test), the "no prompt when nothing excluded" test correctly stayed green. (b) warnExcludedFamilies's guard forced to unconditional return -> exactly 1/183 red (the flag-path warns test), the flag-path "nothing excluded" test correctly stayed green. (c) renderPretty's `if (data.migration.excluded.length > 0)` forced to `if (false)` -> exactly 1/185 red (the new pretty-mode render test), the plain-mode render test correctly stayed green since only the pretty branch was mutated. All three confirm the new tests assert the specific behavior named, not just "something changed" -- and were reverted (confirmed via `git diff` showing no residual mutant hunks) before the final `npm run check` proof below.

`npm run check` does not exist as a script in this repo (checked package.json directly) -- ran the equivalent set instead: `bun run typecheck` (0 errors), `bun run lint` (0 errors; 3 pre-existing warnings in files this branch never touched -- agents.ts, check-package-artifacts.test.ts, shipped-readme-version.test.ts, confirmed via `git status --porcelain` before committing), `bun test` (3208 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail across 101 files), and `lore check --plain` since docs/reference/cli-surface.md was touched (80 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped -- unrelated pre-existing skip count).
